result.title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
result.summary: In Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning, large language models may correctly infer the agent's mental state but fail to use that inference when predicting or judging the agent's subsequent actions. In this work, we investigate whether explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action with rules improves ToM reasoning. We generate concise \textit{if--then} rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks. GRPO with rule generation outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and think reasoning. Moreover, rules generated by larger models ($\geq$3B) provide transferable knowledge that improves downstream performance of GPT-4o-mini. These findings suggest that explicit rules help models bridge the reasoning gap in ToM and support knowledge transfer across models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究用显式 if-then 规则连接感知与行动、并以 GRPO 微调 Qwen2.5 与 Llama3，在四个 ToM 基准上考察能否弥合「正确推断心理状态却未用于行动判断」的缺口，并检验大模型生成规则的跨模型迁移性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「推断正确但未用于输出」的失败诊断与 latents 未被答案使用的信息坍缩问题可能同源，规则生成加 GRPO 的监督形式或可作为 LVR 轨迹训练与贡献分配的借鉴线索，需核查是否涉及推理期状态使用。
